paragraphs: Students who take notes by hand tend to remember lectures better than those who type, a finding often attributed to the pace of writing. Because handwriting is slow, the note-taker cannot transcribe every word and must instead decide what matters and put it in his or her own words. Typists can keep up with the speaker and so often copy sentences nearly verbatim, a practice that demands little thought. The advantage of handwriting may therefore lie not in the pen itself but in the thinking it forces. If that is right, a typist who deliberately paraphrases rather than transcribes should do as well, although I know of no study that has tested this directly.
